about.title: Bishop Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Bishop sits along US-395 where the highway becomes N Main Street, and nearly everything in town — errands, work, the drive north or south — moves through that corridor. In 2025, public records show 14 injury collisions in Bishop, 16 people hurt, and one traffic death. Numbers like that stay small in a town of 3,806, which is exactly why a single loss lands so hard here. When a death was caused by someone else's carelessness — a driver, a property owner, a business, a care provider — California law gives certain family members a civil path to hold that party accountable. A wrongful death claim in Inyo County is separate from any criminal charge the district attorney may bring; it can move forward whether or not a prosecution does. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these claims and works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Bishop Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clear answers on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can tell you quickly whether you are among those who can bring the claim.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched closely
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Connecting early means those dates are tracked from the start.

items.title: Every category of loss is accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. The attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on US-395 near Bishop. Does it matter if a state or county agency was involved?
items.answer: It can matter a great deal. If a public entity such as Caltrans or Inyo County is a potentially responsible party, California requires a government claim to be filed on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. An attorney can sort out who may be responsible and make sure no deadline is missed while your family is still grieving.

items.question: The Inyo County District Attorney is pressing charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and stands on its own, separate from any criminal prosecution. It can proceed whether or not charges are filed or a conviction is reached, and the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court.

items.question: I am a sibling. Can I bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing is limited under California law. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first; siblings and other relatives generally may only file if there are no such survivors or if they were financially dependent on the person who died. An attorney can review your specific situation and explain where you stand.
